title: Suit Eligibility Limits by Programme — Legal Forwarding Agreements
content:
**Legal department schedule — suit terms of the Legal Forwarding Agreements programmes.**

Six programme terms govern suit under a Legal Forwarding Agreement: whether the programme files suits at all, the smallest and largest balance due on which a suit is filed, the calendar days that must remain before the statute-of-limitations expiry date when a suit is authorized, the balance up to which a suit needs no account-by-account client authorization, and the calendar days after a client's suit authorization within which the suit must be filed.

## Schedule

| Programme | Files suits | Smallest balance due for suit | Largest balance due for suit | Days that must remain before limitation expiry at authorization | Preauthorized suit limit | Authorization validity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attorney Demand Program | No | $0.00 | $0.00 | 0 | $0.00 | 0 days |
| Small Claims Suit Program | Yes | $500.00 | $10000.00 | 90 | $2500.00 | 60 days |
| Client-Advanced Cost Suit Program | Yes | $1500.00 | $250000.00 | 180 | $0.00 | 60 days |
| Agency-Advanced Cost Suit Program | Yes | $2500.00 | $100000.00 | 180 | $5000.00 | 60 days |
| Judgment Enforcement Program | No | $0.00 | $0.00 | 0 | $0.00 | 0 days |
| Full-Service Litigation Program | Yes | $1500.00 | $250000.00 | 180 | $10000.00 | 90 days |

Where a programme files no suits, the balance limits read $0.00 and the day counts read 0; those zeros mark the absence of suit, not a limit of zero.

## Definitions of the columns

- **Smallest and largest balance due for suit.** The smallest and the largest balance due on the account on which a suit is filed under the programme. Both figures are themselves within the range: a balance due equal to either figure falls inside it.
- **Days that must remain before limitation expiry.** The calendar days that must remain before the account's statute-of-limitations expiry date when a suit is authorized.
- **Preauthorized suit limit.** The balance at or below which a suit needs no account-by-account client authorization. A limit of $0.00 means every suit needs one.
- **Authorization validity.** The calendar days after a client's suit authorization within which the suit must be filed.

## Boundary readings (hypothetical balances)

| Programme | Hypothetical balance due | Within the suit range? | Account-by-account client authorization needed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small Claims Suit Program | $499.99 | No — below $500.00 | — |
| Small Claims Suit Program | $500.00 | Yes — equal to the smallest figure | No — at or below $2500.00 |
| Small Claims Suit Program | $2500.01 | Yes | Yes — above $2500.00 |
| Small Claims Suit Program | $10000.01 | No — above $10000.00 | — |
| Agency-Advanced Cost Suit Program | $5000.00 | Yes | No — at or below $5000.00 |
| Agency-Advanced Cost Suit Program | $5000.01 | Yes | Yes — above $5000.00 |
| Client-Advanced Cost Suit Program | $1500.00 | Yes | Yes — the limit is $0.00, so every suit needs one |
| Full-Service Litigation Program | $10000.00 | Yes | No — at or below $10000.00 |

## Notes for readers

- The Client-Advanced Cost Suit Program and the Full-Service Litigation Program share the same balance range ($1500.00 to $250000.00) but differ in the preauthorized suit limit ($0.00 against $10000.00) and in authorization validity (60 against 90 days).
- The Small Claims Suit Program requires 90 days to remain before limitation expiry at authorization; the other suit-filing programmes require 180.
